review_categories.name: Technical Review

overlap_detail.G4_EQS: Both read ExplanationCorrect for correctness — Technical checks accounting accuracy, EQS checks educational quality. Same text, different lens. Overlap: ~55%.
overlap_detail.G2_DQS: Difficulty calibration partly depends on technical complexity of the accounting concept. Overlap: ~30%.
overlap_detail.Learner_Safety: DL-030 (wrong answer-key) is both a technical defect and learner-safety risk. Stem-answer consistency checked by both. Overlap: ~50%.
overlap_detail.QA_Board: QA scanners flag structural violations that Technical must adjudicate.

review_categories.unique_contribution: Accounting correctness — the tier-1 concern per CAQS decision hierarchy. Most defensible standalone scope.
review_categories.other_agents_doing_same_check: Learner Safety Agent, Certification Board, Governance Preservation Agent — all independently re-derive CorrectChoice values on the same items (DR-004: 4 agents per session).

review_categories.name: DQS — Distractor Quality Score
what_it_checks: Cueing and pattern analysis (grammatical, length, position bias)

overlap_detail.G1_Technical: Difficulty calibration ties to technical complexity. Overlap: ~30%.
overlap_detail.G4_EQS: Distractor quality evaluated by both — EQS checks if distractors are explained, DQS checks if distractors are psychometrically valid. Same distractors, different criteria. Overlap: ~70% — this is the highest-overlap board pair.
overlap_detail.UIQS: DQS produces distractor quality score; UIQS consumes it as a dimension input. Overlap: ~40%.

review_categories.unique_contribution: Blueprint alignment and Bloom's taxonomy — most unique scope among content boards. Psychometric rules are well-defined.
review_categories.other_agents_doing_same_check: EQS Agent (DR-001: EW per-slot analysis), DL-031 Readiness Agent (S809.2), Difficulty Calibration Agent (S810.1) — all independently score the same distractors.
review_categories.false_negative_rate: HIGH — DL-031: ~500 items systematically mislabeled. DL-032: all 420 case items uniformly Moderate. 0 items labeled Very Difficult, 0 labeled Evaluate.

review_categories.name: EQS — Explanation Quality Score
what_it_checks: EV1-EV8 compliance (min 50 chars, no placeholder, ASC citation)
ExplanationCorrect depth: formula with substitution, business interpretation, exam trap
Choice-specificity verification (each EW field addresses its specific choice)

overlap_detail.G2_DQS: Both read every ExplanationWrong[A-D] slot. EQS checks clarity/completeness, DQS checks trap-engineering. Highest-overlap pair at 70%. An item passing DQS at 90+ is almost guaranteed to pass EQS for the distractor dimension.
overlap_detail.Learner_Safety: DL-008 (non-empty EW[CC]) = explanation structural error. Overlap: 40%.
overlap_detail.QA_Board: QA scanners flag EV violations (50-char threshold, placeholder text). EQS must adjudicate scanner findings.

review_categories.unique_contribution: Instructional quality — writing clarity, educational depth. But 55% of what it checks is already covered by Technical (correctness) or DQS (distractor quality).
review_categories.other_agents_doing_same_check: Technical Accuracy Agent, EW Integrity Agent, Quality Gate Agent, Learner Safety Agent, COSO Citation Agent. DR-002: 3-4 duplicate EC analyses per session.

review_categories.name: UIQS — User Interface Quality Score
what_it_checks: Question rendering correctness (choices display matching content block)
fields_touched: Choices.{A,B,C,D} (rendering layer only — NOT content review of answer correctness)

overlap_detail.QA_Board: Automated UI validation tests overlap. But UIQS does manual verification. Overlap: 15%.

review_categories.unique_contribution: Rendering layer correctness — fundamentally different from content review. Evaluates what the learner sees on screen, not what the answer key says. Most uniquely-scoped board.

ExplanationWrong.description: The single most multiply-audited field in the repository. Every certification session deploys 4-7 agents that independently re-audit the same EW fields for the same 4 defect classes.

boards_and_what_they_check.G1_Technical: EW correctness: does the text contain accounting errors? Is COSO/framework terminology correct? Does the EW text accurately describe why a choice is wrong?
boards_and_what_they_check.G4_EQS: EW quality: is EW ≥50 chars? Is it choice-specific? Does it teach why the choice is wrong? No placeholder/boilerplate (DL-013)? Does it name the accounting principle?
boards_and_what_they_check.G2_DQS: EW distractor engineering: does each EW describe a specific misconception? Are distractors psychometrically valid? Do they discriminate between understanding levels?
boards_and_what_they_check.Learner_Safety: EW structural safety: is EW[CorrectChoice] empty (DL-008)? Are all EW[non-CC] non-empty (DL-026)? Are EW fields addressing the correct choices (DL-010/DL-016)?
boards_and_what_they_check.QA_Board: EW structural compliance: field presence, field emptiness, 50-char minimum, EV rule compliance, governance guard Rule 2 BLOCK enforcement.
boards_and_what_they_check.Certification_Board: EW synthesis: re-verifies ALL above checks before making CERTIFY/HOLD decision. ALL_AGREE requirement means every EW finding is re-checked.
boards_and_what_they_check.Readiness_Board: EW defect count: checks whether DL-008/DL-026 counts are acceptable for session progression.

consolidation_opportunities.description: Produce exactly 2 files per session: DASHBOARD.json (all metrics) and SESSION_SUMMARY.md (executive narrative). All single-purpose reports (EW audit, technical review, etc.) contain ONLY their domain-specific analysis — do NOT repeat portfolio-level metrics.

estimated_reduction.cross_file_metric_redundancy: 85% reduction (from avg 5.3 files per metric to 2 files)

consolidation_opportunities.title: Eliminate redundant per-session DL-008/DL-026/DL-013 scans
consolidation_opportunities.description: The same structural scans are repeated 3-5x per session by different boards. Implement a scan-once, consume-many model: a single agent runs all 3 defect scans, publishes results as shared session artifact, all boards consume.

estimated_reduction.scan_events_per_session: 3 defect classes × 4-5 boards = 12-15 → 3 (single scan per defect class)

total_unique_reviews_possible.description: If every review dimension were genuinely independent (no overlap), how many distinct review passes would be needed?

current_review_count.description: Actual number of review passes per certification wave across all boards
current_review_count.average_review_passes_per_item: 15-28 agent examinations per item per wave (9-11 boards × 1.5-3x re-examination per board)
current_review_count.example_S809: 28 agent spawns examining 38 Domain E seeds
current_review_count.total_agent_examinations_across_800_seri: ~200-300 agent-level review passes just for Domain E seed certification, for items that had 0 content changes between examinations

duplication_ratio.description: Ratio of actual review passes to possible unique review passes
duplication_ratio.across_4_session_chain_S809_to_S810_1: 56 agent passes / 9 possible = 6.2:1 duplication ratio (the same 38 items examined 56 times, 0 writes performed)
duplication_ratio.field_level_EW: 4-7 agents examining the same EW fields per session = 4-7:1 duplication ratio on the single most multiply-examined field
duplication_ratio.scan_level_DL008: 22 scan events / 8 genuinely needed = 2.75:1 duplication ratio
duplication_ratio.scan_level_DL026: 18 scan events / 6 genuinely needed = 3.0:1 duplication ratio
duplication_ratio.report_level: 7 files per metric / 2 files needed = 3.5:1 duplication ratio
duplication_ratio.overall_weighted_duplication_ratio: 2.5:1 — for every genuinely needed review pass, 2.5 passes are performed

financial_equivalent.agent_hours_wasted_across_800_series: ~50-80 hours of redundant agent examination time (read-only sessions that produced no new findings beyond what the first session established)
financial_equivalent.notes: At current trajectory of 11.7 files/session, the 1,212-file repository would grow to ~2,000 files after completing Domain E/F certification if report duplication is not addressed.

scan_once.description: Run exactly one pre-flight structural scan per session using the definitive AM-1 Function Constructor Parse methodology. Scan output: per-item defect inventory (DL-008/026/018/025 counts, certified count, EW integrity, DL-013 boilerplate status). Result: 1 scan replaces 12-15 current per-session scans.
scan_once.prerequisites: AM-1 parser adopted as standard. All boards consume single pre-flight output.

review_once.description: Each review dimension (technical, psychometric, instructional, structural) is evaluated exactly once per item per certification wave. The merged Quality Board (CO-002) ensures 3 agents cover all 10 CAQS dimensions in a single pass. No cross-board re-verification of the same field.
review_once.prerequisites: Quality Board consolidation (CO-002). Delta-based review (CO-004) for subsequent waves.

consume_many.description: All governance processes consume the shared Quality Board verdict. Session Gate Board reads Quality output as prerequisite. Certification Board reads Quality + Session Gate as evidence package. Pre-delivery safety check reads Quality output + excludes known-defective QIDs. Single source of truth for all downstream consumers.
consume_many.quantified_reduction: Current: 7 downstream consumers independently re-verify. Target: 7 consumers read from shared quality verdict.
consume_many.prerequisites: Trust model: all consumers trust Quality Board verdict. ALL_AGREE consensus model inherited from S313 Certification Board.

total_estimated_reduction.overall_efficiency_gain: 50-75% reduction in total agent time per certification wave

top_findings.finding: ExplanationWrong fields are examined 4-7 times per session by different agents examining identical defect classes (DL-008, DL-026, DL-013) and reaching identical conclusions 95%+ of the time.
top_findings.impact: Single largest source of agent-time waste. DR-001: 4-6 redundant agent-spawns per session. In S809's 28-agent deployment, ~20% of agent capacity (5-6 agents) was duplicate EW checking. Across the 800-series, ~30-40 agent-spawns purely for redundant EW re-examination.

top_findings.finding: 4 sessions (S809→S809.1→S809.2→S810.1, 56 agent-spawns, 39 report files) examined the same 38 Domain E seeds without a single pack-file write. All converged on the same finding: 'needs EW authoring.'
top_findings.impact: The most egregious single chain of redundancy. DR-007: 3 wasted sessions, ~45 unnecessary agent-spawns, 28 unnecessary report files. The only new finding (CC discrepancy on 5 seeds) could have been found in S809's initial pass with proper methodology.

top_findings.finding: EQS + DQS boards overlap at ~70% on ExplanationWrong evaluation — the highest board-pair overlap in the 9-board structure. Both read every EW[A-D] slot per item and apply overlapping criteria (clarity vs. trap-engineering).
top_findings.impact: An item that passes DQS at 90+ is almost guaranteed to pass EQS for the distractor dimension. The EQS's unique contribution is EC depth assessment and writing clarity — both of which Technical Review already partially covers.

top_findings.finding: 22 separate DL-008 scanning events across ~15 sessions, each deploying 3-5 agents for identical structural checks. DL-026: 18 events. DL-013: 12 events. Certified count: 25+ events.
top_findings.impact: Combined ~65-80 scanning events that could be reduced to ~20 (per-session pre-flight scans). The root cause is that no shared scan output exists — each board distrusts every other board's counts and re-derives independently, especially after DL-029 false positives contaminated multiple reference documents.

top_findings.finding: 7 separate report files per session redundantly report the same portfolio-level metrics (certified count, Domain E count, EW integrity, UIQS score, governance guard status). Core 15 metrics spread across an average of 5.3 files each.
top_findings.impact: 1,212 report files for 178 sessions. 65% are one-off artifacts. If report consumption were consolidated (DASHBOARD + SUMMARY only, domain-specific reports without metric repetition), total file count would drop to ~400-500 without information loss.

top_findings.finding: 80% of items unchanged between certification waves (S200 Agent I). Certification Board re-examines all items regardless.
top_findings.impact: Delta-based review (CO-004) would reduce certification review time by 77%. SHA-256 per-item content hashing would enable automated 'unchanged = inherits prior verdict' without manual re-examination.

top_findings.finding: Overall weighted duplication ratio: 2.5:1 — for every genuinely needed review pass, 2.5 passes are performed. Peak: 6.2:1 on the S809 chain.
top_findings.impact: The consolidated 4-board, 6-agent architecture (S200 Board Consolidation) reduces this to approximately 1.2:1 — near-optimal with cross-board ALL_AGREE consensus retained.
